evidence.note: After the first real training runs, agent applies patches then drops COMPILE, adds PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True, and lowers TRAIN_BATCH_TOKENS while raising ITERS (5000→7000→10000) — targeted responses to run/memory problems, not blind re-runs.
Architecture sweep: varies MODEL_DIM/NUM_KV_HEADS/HIDDEN_DIM/NUM_LAYERS (kv=5 vs 10, hidden 1728/1536/1408), with CPU-only param-count checks — trading width/depth against the size budget.
Quantization group-size sweep (Q_GROUP_SIZE 512/256/768) with a group_test.ptz probe — isolating the quant lever to gauge size vs accuracy tradeoff.

Introduces CKPT_CODEC=lzma as a new size lever, then systematically ablates Q_SMALL_GROUP_PATTERNS (mixed-precision on tok_embeddings, w1/w2/w3, layers.13/14/15) — treating the size↔accuracy frontier as the object of optimization, buying accuracy within the byte cap.
Converges on chosen architecture for a final training run, then packs with lzma/group-size and verifies compile + file size — integrating the tuned levers into a final submission.

reasoning: The command evolution shows the agent diagnosing distinct binding constraints (memory → expandable_segments/batch cuts; capacity → arch sweeps; size vs accuracy → quant group size, lzma codec, and per-layer mixed-precision ablation) and changing the specific right lever each time, with single-variable isolation across many falsified probes — matching anchor 8's 'trade depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap' and approaching the level-10 frontier-optimization pattern. I hold at 8 rather than higher because the log contains no observations or prose, so I cannot verify that dead-ends were explicitly diagnosed and abandoned via reasoning rather than inferred from the highly systematic sweep structure.
